channel.title: The Grant Desk - Prizes and Awards, US, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Prizes and Awards, US, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Tag! Queer Shorts Festival 2027: Call for Submissions (Portland) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Tag! Queer Shorts Festival
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Award categories with cash prizes (amounts not stated): Hispanic/Latine Creativity, Power of Community, Best Erotic Short and Radical Futures Student Film, plus a Festival Director's Award. Modest submission fees on FilmFreeway; fee waivers for historically excluded communities and filmmakers from countries that criminalize queer identities, and discount codes for Pacific Northwest filmmakers.

Tag! invites LGBTQIA+ filmmakers to submit finished shorts of 15 minutes or under, including credits, in any genre (theme for 2027: "You're It!"). About 40 to 45 shorts are selected. English captions are required; films made with generative AI are not programmed; no works in progress.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: AT&T Untold Stories 2027 (Tribeca Festival): USD 1.2 million film production prize (closes 18 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Tribeca Festival and AT&T
Deadline: 18 Jan 2027
Award: One winner receives USD 1,200,000 to produce the film; the four other finalists receive USD 15,000 grants each. No entry fee.

AT&T Untold Stories, now in its 10th year, is a production prize run by the Tribeca Festival and AT&T that funds a feature film from an underrepresented filmmaker. Industry judges select five projects; their filmmakers pitch to a jury of media professionals at the 2027 Tribeca Festival in June.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Hillman Prizes 2027 for Journalism (incl. Broadcast and Documentary) (closes 30 Jan 2027)
item.description:
The Sidney Hillman Foundation
Deadline: 30 Jan 2027
Award: USD 5,000 honorarium and a certificate for each Hillman Prize winner. No entry fee.

The Hillman Prizes honour journalism in service of the common good, with priority for work with US impact.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Van Alen Institute: Re:Paris Prize, USD 35,000 travel research fellowship on design in Africa and its diaspora (US-based applicants) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Van Alen Institute
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026
Award: USD 35,000 travel fellowship; one US-based winner selected through this open call (two Africa-based winners were selected via the 2026 Pan-African Biennale).

The Re:Paris Prize, run by Van Alen Institute, funds research into how design plays a transformative role in Africa and its diaspora. Each winner receives a USD 35,000 travel fellowship for field research that requires international travel to connect with experts and opportunities.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Oregon Media Arts Fellowship 2026 (two USD 5,000 awards for Oregon media artists)
item.description: Portland Art Museum (PAM CUT) and Oregon Arts Commission · deadline 15 Nov 2026 · Two fellowships of USD 5,000 each, no matching funds required; paid within two months of notification. No application fee.

item.title: J. Anthony Lukas Work-in-Progress Awards 2027
item.description: Columbia Journalism School and the Nieman Foundation · deadline 03 Dec 2026 · Two awards of USD 25,000 each. No entry fee for the Work-in-Progress awards.
